learning_outcomes.text: Knows the fundamental concepts of entrepreneurship and its framework at national and European levels.
Understands the relationship between engineering activity and the valorisation of innovations through entrepreneurial initiatives.
Has knowledge about business legislation, intellectual property protection, resources, and business development strategies.
Knows the principles of personal management, career planning, and entrepreneurial skill development.
Understands the stages of initiating, planning, and managing a business, including the development of a business plan.
Identifies business ideas and validates their market potential, using economic and legislative analysis tools.
Develops business plans and financing strategies for their implementation.
Applies marketing and promotion concepts for the valorisation of products/services.
Drafts relevant documents (business plan, CV, presentation) adapted to the entrepreneurial context.
Actively participates in simulations and practical exercises aimed at initiating and managing a business.
Demonstrates initiative and innovative spirit in identifying and exploiting business opportunities.
Assumes responsibility for substantiating entrepreneurial decisions, respecting ethical and legal principles.
Works effectively in a team, contributing to the development of a constructive and collaborative climate.
Demonstrates autonomy in documenting and applying acquired knowledge to real or simulated situations.
Develops critical thinking and adaptability to the dynamic requirements of the market and economic environment.

syllabus_topics: Theories and practices of entrepreneurial education.
The entrepreneur and the phenomenon of entrepreneurship.
Psychological and sociological perspective of entrepreneurship.
Influence of entrepreneurial education on entrepreneurial attitude and intention.
Creativity and innovation: the intersection between theory and practice.
Forms of education and the importance of entrepreneurial education at the individual and societal level.
The entrepreneur as a person and the phenomenon of entrepreneurship.
teaching_methods: Centred on developing critical thinking, creativity and decision-making capacity
assessment_rules: Students must achieve a minimum grade of 5 for both the Colloquium and the Laboratory activity to pass the course. All laboratory works must be completed, with recovery allowed for only one outstanding laboratory work. Passing requires the technical-economic and financial substantiation of entrepreneurial decision-making and technological design, understanding and correct use of entrepreneurial education concepts, and the ability to use specific terminology for initiating and designing a business.
